1.label: very_easy
1.summary: A single outline uses one ink and no loop. The full coordinate grid and long-lived stroke reveal make each primitive directly measurable before it disappears.
1.natural_language: Inspect the transient reference strokes, then arrange punch cards to draw the same single-ink outline and certify the plate.

2.label: easy
2.summary: A closed five- or six-stroke seal must be expressed with one repeat block because the tape is shorter than its unrolled program. The full grid remains visible.
2.natural_language: Inspect the repeating transient seal, compress its geometry into a loop, proof the drawing, and certify the plate.

3.label: medium
3.summary: The baseline compound seal contains two differently coloured closed figures separated by an invisible pen-up relocation. Both figures require loop compression, and only the major grid remains.
3.natural_language: Inspect the UV reference until you can reconstruct every transient stroke. Build a compact two-ink punch-card program, proof it, then certify the plate.

4.label: hard
4.summary: Two differently structured loops share turtle state, followed by a third-colour accent reached through another hidden relocation. Only sparse registration marks remain.
4.natural_language: Recover the three-part seal from its transient scan, preserve heading and pen state across both loops and relocations, then proof and certify it.

5.label: very_hard
5.summary: A nested-loop rosette, an eight-stroke star, and a separate triangular stamp share three inks and two invisible relocations. The reference field has no coordinate grid.
5.natural_language: Integrate the full transient forgery master, infer its nested repetition and hidden relocations, then build, proof, and certify the three-ink program.

simplified.summary: Click a command card to append it to the tape; labelled arrow buttons move existing cards.

full.summary: Drag command cards directly from the drawer into the tape and drag tape cards to reorder them.
